name: Caterpillar Global Mining - South Milwaukee WI Plant
type: Manufacturing plant (large mining equipment - electric rope shovels, draglines)

fieldNotes.location: Roster lat/lng (GEOMETRIC_CENTER, movedMeters 234) sits on the campus. Confirmed: the historic former Bucyrus heavy-equipment works in South Milwaukee, operated by Caterpillar Global Mining since 2011; produces massive Cat electric rope shovels (7495 series) and draglines. Address 1100 Milwaukee Ave. Locked center on the main building corridor at 42.9127,-87.8615.
fieldNotes.type: Heavy-manufacturing / fabrication complex, NOT a distribution facility. The site assembles room-sized mining-shovel components; it has large open paved assembly/staging yards rather than a conventional bank of loading-dock doors.
fieldNotes.truckGate: The entire complex is enclosed by a perimeter wall/fence (concrete wall visible along Milwaukee Ave in Street View). Vehicles enter via controlled gated openings in the wall. Set true.
fieldNotes.guardShack: A small structure with signage sits at the main entrance gate on the W/N side; consistent with a security/guard checkpoint for a fenced industrial works. Marked true at medium confidence - flagged.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: At least two gated openings in the perimeter wall (W/N side near the parking lots, and another along the street) - estimated 2, flagged.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Heavy-fabrication plant - large oversized bay/shop doors, not a regular dock-door rhythm. Estimated 0-10 conventional dock equivalents, flagged.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Large open paved yards for staging oversized components, not marked trailer-parking stalls; few standard trailers visible. dropArea 0-10, dropYard false.
fieldNotes.railServed: TRUE - multiple rail spurs run directly into the property along the W side; oversized shovel components ship by rail. Clearly visible in z17-z18 imagery.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Campus of ~8 large connected/adjacent heavy-industrial buildings spanning a long N-S corridor.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Urban - the works is embedded in the dense South Milwaukee residential street grid, houses directly across the street on all sides.
fieldNotes.backupSensitive: The complex fronts directly onto public city streets with minimal setback; a truck queue at a gate would spill onto a public road - backupSensitive true.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Multiple separate gated openings in the perimeter wall on different street frontages - treated as separate entry/exit.
